answer: Bind each identity to one sealed replica: verifiers pull random sectors of a copy encoded with that identity's key, so it occupies its identity like one berth at a wharf. N clones need N full replicas across the whole reward horizon, each earning at most one share; the fleet profits only while a share outruns replica upkeep, a measurable bound, not faith. Assumes slow-to-fake sealing and bonded samplers that slash missed sectors. Cheap rented disks still sail past this reef.
